cost_rule: Mana = Power Level. Casters and Channelers subtract Character Level / 6, rounded down, minimum 1 Mana. Paid win or lose. Surge and Effect boxes are never discounted. Basic Cast is free.

sources.name: Arcane
text: Any setting with a magic tradition. TL 1+.
Components: Gestures, spoken words, runes, ritual components. Always visible.
Learning: Arcane powers can be taught, copied, and learned from written sources.
Disruption: Silenced prevents verbal components (Cast DC 10 to continue). Restrained at -2.
Void: Using Void Effect via Arcane requires Corruption check DC 14 regardless of Surge level. | Visible to others: Any bystander can see Arcane in use.
Counterable: Arcane can be Abjured. Spirit/Shamanic cannot.

The most common Power Source in fantasy settings. Arcane magic is systematic — it follows rules that can be discovered and codified. A character with Arcane can, in principle, teach another character Arcane.

sources.name: Divine
text: Any setting with a faith tradition. TL 1+.
Components: Holy symbols, prayer, laying on hands. Faith-powered.
Source: Power comes from genuine faith, not the deity directly. A crisis of faith Drains Mana -2 until resolved.
Void: Divine characters who use Void Effect must make a Corruption check DC 12 (lower than Arcane — doctrine may permit it).
Healing: Only Power Source with native access to Healing Effect at no additional cost flag. | Cannot be Silenced: Prayer is internal — Silenced condition does not prevent Divine use.
Abjurable: Divine can be Abjured. Innate cannot.

Divine power does not require the deity's conscious approval for each action — it is stored faith, not a direct phone line. A character can use Divine powers while their deity sleeps, is absent, or does not exist.

sources.name: Innate
text: Any setting. TL 1+. ML 0 possible for subtle innate abilities.
Components: None. Biological, bloodline, or cosmic gift. No words, no gestures.
Learning: Cannot be taught. Cannot be copied. Narrative source defines what is possible.
Suppression: Innate cannot be Abjured. It can be Negated by specific powers designed for it.
Versatility: Uses whatever Ability fits the specific power. A fire-blooded character uses STR for fire breath; a telepath uses INT. | No Corruption check: Innate Void use does not trigger Corruption.
Setting-specific: GM defines the narrative source at character creation.

Innate is the broadest Power Source — it covers dragons, mutants, superheroes, blessed bloodlines, alien physiology, and anything else that cannot be explained by training or faith. The specific Ability is chosen at character creation and does not change.

sources.name: Psionic
text: Settings with ML 2+. Present in high-tech settings as standard.
Components: Silent. No visible manifestation. No words, no gestures, no components.
Mindless immunity: Creatures with no Intellect (Constructs, undead without minds) may be immune to Psychic Effects at 1-3 boxes via Psionic. GM adjudicates.
Suppression: Psionic cannot be Silenced. It can be blocked by psionic shielding (specific powers or TL 9+ technology).
Social: Psionic is the only Power Source that can be used in social situations without detection. | Undetectable: No visible tell unless the character chooses to make one.
Detection: Other psionics can detect psionic activity at ACU DC 13.

The silent Power Source. Psionic characters frequently have to decide whether to reveal their abilities or use them covertly. In settings where psionics are feared or regulated (Shadowrun, Dark Sun, many sci-fi settings), this becomes a major character and social factor.

sources.name: Spirit / Shamanic
text: Settings with animist or shamanic traditions. TL 1+.
Components: Varies — ritual objects, offerings, spoken bargains, drumming, dance.
Source: Power is bargained or gifted from external entities (spirits, ancestors, nature forces). The power is not yours alone.
Entity agenda: The GM may introduce entity complications. A spirit that granted power may later want something in return.
Abjure immunity: Spirit/Shamanic powers cannot be Abjured (the spirit is not casting — the character is relaying). | Entity relationship: Character must maintain relationship with source entity.
No Void Corruption: Spirit/Shamanic Void use does not trigger the Arcane Corruption check.

Distinct from Divine: Divine power comes from the character's own faith. Shamanic power comes from an agreement with something outside. The entity can renege. The entity can upgrade the deal. The entity has opinions about how its power is used.

sources.name: Weird Science
text: TL 5+. Cannot be used at TL 1-4 without GM exception.
Components: Gadgets, serums, devices, formulae. Always has a physical component.
Preparation: Most Weird Science powers require preparation time outside of combat (GM discretion, typically 10 minutes to 1 hour for complex devices).
Destruction: Physical gadgets can be targeted (DR 0, Stamina 6 for a standard device). If destroyed, the power is unavailable until rebuilt.
Reproducible: Weird Science can be explained and replicated by anyone with sufficient Intellect and materials. It is technology, not magic. | No Corruption: Weird Science has no Corruption track.
TL-limited: Specific devices only available at appropriate Technology Level.

Weird Science is technology that should not work yet does — it is D&D's Artificer, GURPS' gadgeteer, Shadowrun' s technomancer adjacent. Distinct from Arcane because it is repeatable, physical, and teachable to anyone regardless of Ability. The character's Intellect determines reliability and power, not some innate gift.

sources.name: Alchemical
text: TL 3+. Pre-industrial chemistry settings, fantasy apothecary traditions.
Components: Prepared substances — potions, bombs, salves, reagents. Must be crafted in advance.
Preparation: All Alchemical powers are crafted out of combat. Activation in combat is instantaneous (draw and use).
Supply limit: Characters carry a limited number of prepared substances (GM sets inventory cap, typically 3-6 per scene).
No Mana pool cost: Alchemical activation costs Stamina (physical exertion of use), not Mana. The preparation was the hard part.

sources.name: Blood Magic
text: Any TL / ML with a tradition of sacrifice. Often restricted or forbidden.
Cost structure: Instead of spending Mana, Blood Magic powers cost Stamina boxes directly. 1 Stamina = 1 Mana for Power purposes.
No Mana required: A Blood Magic character does not need a Mana pool. Stamina serves as the fuel.
Pool risk: Stamina spent on Blood Magic counts as damage taken — it crosses boxes and may trigger Hurt/Injured thresholds.
Corruption: Using Blood Magic on an unwilling target's blood (forced sacrifice) requires a Corruption check DC 16.

sources.name: Chi / Ki
text: Any TL. Requires trained discipline — not a gift.
Components: None. Internal. Breath control, body movement, trained focus.
Source: Trained discipline, not bloodline gift. Anyone can learn with sufficient time (GM sets training requirements).
Vs Innate: Innate = you were born with it. Chi = you trained for it. Mechanically similar, narratively opposite.
Suppression: Chi cannot be Abjured. It can be disrupted by specific anti-ki techniques (other Chi practitioners or specific Powers).

sources.name: Cybernetic
text: TL 8+. Implanted technology — not carried, not destroyable without surgery.
Components: Implanted technology. No preparation required — always active or on-demand.
Vs Weird Science: Weird Science = external gadgets. Cybernetic = implanted. Cybernetics cannot be dropped, pickpocketed, or targeted separately without surgery.
Disruption: Electric Effect at 3+ boxes can disrupt Cybernetic powers (system short-out). EMP disables all Cybernetic powers for the scene.
Humanity cost: High-Cybernetic characters may develop social penalties at GM discretion (TL 9+ settings with Humanity mechanics).

sources.name: Demonic / Pact-Bound
sources.pools_text: Mana / Resolve (and sometimes Stamina — see notes)
text: Any setting with supernatural entities willing to make deals.
Components: Varies by pact terms. Often involves a symbol, trigger word, or ritual gesture.
Source: Power granted by a demonic, infernal, or significantly powerful entity. The deal was bad. The character may not know how bad.
Corruption: Every use of Pact-Bound powers requires a Corruption check (DC 10 + Power Level). This is not negotiable. It is in the contract.
Vs Shamanic: Spirit/Shamanic = entity can be reasoned with. Demonic = entity has a fixed agenda and the contract is non-negotiable.

sources.name: Nature / Primal
text: Settings with a living natural world. TL 1-5 primarily; present at any TL with GM approval.
Components: Touch, proximity to natural material, spoken communion. Never requires manufactured components.
Source: Direct relationship with the living world — not through intermediary entities. The land itself, not spirits of the land.
Vs Shamanic: Spirit/Shamanic = relationship with spirits OF nature. Nature/Primal = relationship WITH nature directly.
Restriction: Nature/Primal powers are diminished in environments without natural material (urban TL 8+ settings: -1 to all Nature/Primal rolls). Fully functional in wilderness.

sources.name: Runic / Inscription
text: TL 2+. Settings with written language and a runic tradition.
Components: Written runes, sigils, inscriptions. Always physical — a rune that is not written does not exist.
Preparation: Runic powers must be prepared in advance. Activation in the moment of need is free (the rune fires). No improvisation.
Duration: A rune activates once and is spent. Permanent runes (etched in stone/metal) cost double Mana on preparation.
Cannot improvise: A Runic character cannot create a new effect in combat. They bring what they prepared.

weird.source: Book of Genres, Weird Magic. Tainted is tracked as Corruption (DECISIONS.md).
weird.when: Whenever you cast a Weird Magic Power, roll d20 after the Power's success or failure is resolved. The result applies on top of the normal Power effect. A Bane (natural 1) on the cast, or a Backlash or Revelation result, adds 1 Corruption.

table.name: Backlash
table.effect: The Power also targets the caster at half effect. Add 1 Corruption immediately.

table.name: Bleed
table.effect: The Power leaves a visible mark on the caster — a scorch, a sigil, a color in the eye. Narrative only; the GM tracks it and may use it later.

table.name: Echo
table.effect: The Power fires again next round at the same target. No Action or pool cost required.

table.name: Drain
table.effect: The pool cost drains from a random pool. Roll d20: 1–7 Mana, 8–14 Stamina, 15–20 Resolve.

table.name: Surge Free
table.effect: The Power gains 1 free Surge box this cast at no cost.

table.name: Stable
table.effect: No additional effect. The Weird was quiet this time.

table.name: Shift
table.effect: The Effect type changes to an adjacent type. GM and player agree on adjacency (Fire→Electric, Psychic→Void, Toxic→Cold, etc.).

table.name: Revelation
table.effect: The caster briefly perceives something they were not meant to see. The GM narrates a fragment of forbidden knowledge. Mark 1 Resolve box. Add 1 Corruption.

weird.fallout_when: On a Weird Magic cast, a natural 1 while Surging 3+ boxes is Weird Fallout instead of the normal Surge Fallout. Roll d20:

fallout.name: Uncontrolled outward
fallout.effect: The Power manifests in the environment (as Arcane Fallout). Add 1 Corruption.

fallout.name: Inward
fallout.effect: The caster gains Removed (Spirit) for the rest of the scene (as Spiritual Fallout). Add 1 Corruption.

fallout.name: Unravelling
fallout.effect: The Power fails completely — no effect, pool cost still paid. Add 1 Corruption.

fallout.name: Something notices
fallout.effect: The GM introduces a supernatural consequence in the next scene — an entity drawn by the signal, a shift in local reality, an uninvited presence. Add 2 Corruption.

notes: Weird Control (Willpower, DC 14): try to direct or suppress a Weird Table result before it resolves — choose between the rolled result and a re-roll. Succeeding twice on Weird Control in one scene adds 1 Corruption.
Weird Read (Acuity): after 3+ Weird rolls in a session, the GM gives insight into what the Weird is doing.
Witnesses to Weird Magic, allies included, make a Horror Check DC 12 when they see it cast. The caster is exempt.

The Weird Role changes these rolls: roll twice and choose (Step 1), Revelation marks no Resolve (Step 2), declare a result once per scene (Step 3), choose the Drain pool (Step 4), redirect Backlash to a visible target (Step 5).

making_rule: Start at Power Level 1: one target, Near range or closer, instant, doing one small thing. Add +1 for each upgrade. On a hit, cross boxes equal to the overage or the Power Level, whichever is higher, up to the Hit Cap.
limits_rule: Tough targets: a Power that controls or removes a foe without crossing boxes must be at least PL 3 against a Rival, PL 4 against an Antagonist, PL 5 against a Boss. Minions can be affected at any Level. Ask the GM only for story-changing magic.
cantrip_rule: A cantrip is PL 1, Close or Touch, one target: free with Cast or Channel at rank 2+, otherwise it costs normal Mana.
spell_rule: Every spell can be cast at Level 1 in a small form. Choose any Step you have unlocked; its Power Level is its cost. On a hit, cross boxes equal to the overage or the Step's PL, whichever is higher.
